claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex, who is 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 19 years old, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether they are still in approved education or training. Let me ask you about their current situation:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following?**
- Full-time non-advanced education (e.g., A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3)
- An approved training course (not paid for by an employer)
- Or neither of the above

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in college doing their A-levels. They're in full-time education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 19 and in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels), they may still qualify for Child Benefit.

I have a couple more questions:

**Does Alex live with you, or do they live elsewhere?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just one more important question:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and upbringing (such as providing food, housing, and looking after their welfare)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex's other parent also lives with us and they're the one who claims Child Benefit for Alex already.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Ah, I see. That's an important detail.

If Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, then only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child at any given time. 

**Is your question about whether you could claim Child Benefit instead of Alex's other parent, or were you perhaps thinking of claiming for a different child?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I was just wondering if I would be eligible to claim it myself. So does that mean I'm not eligible because the other parent is already claiming?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's correct. Under Child Benefit rules, **only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time**. Since Alex's other parent is already receiving Child Benefit for Alex, you would not be eligible to make a separate claim for the same child.

However, there are a couple of things to note:

1. **You could claim instead** – If you and Alex's other parent agreed, they could stop their claim and you could start a new one. Only one of you can claim at any given time, but it doesn't have to be the person currently claiming.

2. **If you disagree about who should claim** – HMRC will usually pay the Child Benefit to the person the child lives with. Since you all live together, HMRC would decide based on who has main responsibility for the child.

Would you like me to provide a formal eligibility assessment based on your current circumstances (i.e., that someone else is already claiming for Alex)? Or do you have any other children you'd like me to assess eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's all I needed to know. So just to be clear - I'm not eligible because someone else is already claiming for Alex, right?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Based on the official guidance, I can now provide you with a formal eligibility assessment.

Yes, that's correct. While Alex would otherwise meet the criteria for Child Benefit (being under 20 and in full-time approved education), the key rule is that **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child** at any one time. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you are not eligible to make a separate claim.

Let me provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
To summarise:

**Eligibility Assessment for Child Benefit**

| Child | Eligible? | Reason |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Alex | **No** | Although Alex meets the age and education criteria (under 20 and in full-time approved education), another person is already claiming Child Benefit for them. Only one person can claim per child. |

If circumstances change in the future—for example, if you and Alex's other parent agree that you should be the one to claim instead—you could apply once they stop their claim.

I hope this helps clarify things! If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.
